Collection 01

Ornamental Fish

Fish bring movement and colour to a composition. This family is presented as studies of form and finnage, with selection framed as questions to discuss rather than a stock list.

Prepare a fish enquiry All collections

Studies

Colour and form, side by side.

Two illustrative studies. Descriptions note what is visible in the image; they are not confirmed species or available stock.

Selection considerations

What shapes a fish selection

Framed as questions for a conversation. Care requirements vary by fish and should be confirmed for each case.

i.

Colour and finnage

Is colour meant to lead the display or accent it? Long fins read beautifully in calm water but change how a fish fits with others.

ii.

Form and movement

Tall, slow-moving forms suit open water; small, quick fish bring life to planted edges. Movement is part of the composition.

iii.

Community fit

Which inhabitants are already there or planned? Temperament and pace matter as much as appearance.

iv.

Display context

Viewing distance, lighting and background colour all change how a fish is seen. A dark planted scape and a bright open tank ask for different choices.

Enquiry context

Preparing a fish enquiry

A short, specific brief makes the first conversation useful. The contact page will start with ornamental fish selected.

Prepare a fish enquiry
  • Display size, layout and where it will be viewed from
  • Current or planned inhabitants
  • The look you are after: colour, movement, calm or lively
  • An approximate quantity range and timing
  • Whether plants or driftwood are part of the same plan
